title: add boil --search flag
description:
search will try to find the minimal set of lines that satisfies tests, not just files

the current boil implementation tends to use "restore_full" too much, assuming that an entire file's content is required to get tests passing.

"boil --search" will restore entire files only until tests pass. Then it will backtrack, restarting from the beginning and only restoring lines from files that are known to be part of the final solution.


So if after the first pass, a file remains deleted, then the search knows to completely ignore that file on the second pass.
On the second pass, the search must intelligently use the src_repair feature to restore syntax to files. No more full restores.


write two different plans of attack for how to accomplish this search. Ask for approval before continuing to implementation.

title: boil --finish should only delete boil session, not .boil directory
test_after_is_subset fails on binary .o files
description:
The test_after_is_subset test checks that after/ file content is a subsequence of before/ content.
This works for text files but fails for binary files like .o object files because they differ between builds even with identical source code.

.o files should NEVER be committed.
they are generated by the build process, but they should be deleted before comparing repos

:bash$ find before -name "*.o"
:bash$ find after -name "*.o"
after/mksignames.o
after/buildsignames.o
after/buildversion.o


Somehow these .o files got commited when the after/ directory was created.


I think we need to recreate the after/ directory from a fresh boiling of before/
and we need to make sure the before directory has no generated files in it when copied to after/
